messages:
alex: quick design question — we need a consistent cross-lang shape for paginated streaming + retries. do we push a streaming iterator that auto-retries or give explicit resume tokens to callers?

jasper: +1 we should pick one pattern. streaming + hidden retries feels magical but can hide correctness issues for idempotent vs non-idempotent operations.

maria: my vote is explicit resume tokens for non-idempotent flows. for pure reads (list objects, search) streaming with automatic retry is fine.

sam: agree with maria. also think ergonomics differ by language: TS devs expect async iterators, py wants generator/aiter, go wants channel or explicit pager. how do we unify surface?

jasper: proposal: expose three primitives across SDKs -> 1) simple paged list (sync/async) that returns pages + next_token, 2) a convenience streaming iterator built on top of (1) that can auto-retry only idempotent pages, and 3) a low-level continue-from-token API for apps that need deterministic control.

anya: that maps well to existing usage patterns. nuance: what counts as "idempotent"? listing is idempotent but some search endpoints might mutate metrics or counters. need an explicit flag from server or model spec.

alex: good point. we could require endpoints to declare retry-safety metadata in the model/service catalog (like `retry: safe|unsafe|partial`). SDKs consult that and enable auto-retry only when safe.

maria: implementation detail: streaming iterator should surface a small backoff/retry policy config: {max_retries, base_ms, max_ms, retry_on} and default to conservative values. devs can override.

sam: what about transport-level ambiguity? e.g., websocket streaming vs unary+cursor. If a streaming transport disconnects mid-stream, we need a portable resume token scheme. server must emit opaque resume cursors frequently.

jasper: exactly. resume token semantics: cursor MUST encode server-side position and be usable from paged list API. design rule: resume_token + page_size => deterministic resume. document that token is opaque.

anya: corner case: partial results in last page (server-side batching) -> token should point to next slice start. clients should not assume any token format.

alex: API sketch (TS):
```ts
// high level streaming convenience
for await (const item of client.listItemsStream({filter})) {
  // item-level iteration, auto-retry enabled only if service.retry == 'safe'
}

// low level page + token
const page = await client.listItems({page_size: 100, page_token: 'abc'});
// page.items, page.next_page_token
```

maria: in python similar: iterator = client.list_items_stream(...); async for i in iterator: ... and low-level: client.list_items(page_size=100, page_token=..). keep names consistent across SDKs.

sam: go should provide Pager struct with Next(ctx) (returns items, error) and Resume(token) factory. keep zero-conf convenience via NewPager which wraps retry logic only when allowed.

jasper: retry policy shape should be shared across SDKs. maybe a serialized RetryConfig that travels in SDKs: ["max_retries:3","backoff:exponential","retry_codes:[<connectivity>]"]. keep it simple.

anya: tests: put integration tests that simulate transport disconnect and assert that resume token + page_size yields identical stream as uninterrupted run. also test behavior when service marks endpoint unsafe (should error instead of retrying).

alex: one more ops note: telemetry — emit events when SDK performs an automatic resume/retry (count, latency, trigger) so Console can surface regression hotspots. add opt-out for privacy-sensitive customers.

maria: docs: one page called "Pagination & Stream Resume" with examples per language + table of retry safety rules. and a migration note for older SDKs.

sam: sounds good. next steps: jasper open a tiny RFC PR with the three-primitives approach + token semantics + retry-config shape. i'll start implement stubs for TS + python.

jasper: will do. tagging @deploy-bot to run the cross-sdk compatibility test matrix when we have stubs. :rocket:

deploy-bot: CI job queued: cross-sdk-pager-matrix (job id: 7721)

alex: thanks all — we've got a direction. low-risk, explicit control path for correctness + ergonomic convenience layers.
